arxiv-2112-08445.creator: Tamas G. Molnar, Adam K. Kiss
arxiv-2112-08445.description: Abstract Endowing nonlinear systems with safe behavior is increasingly important in modern control. This task is particularly challenging for real-life control systems that operate in dynamically changing environments. This paper develops a framework for safety-critical control in dynamic environments, by establishing the notion of environmental control barrier functions (ECBFs) .

Abstract : This multi-disciplinary case study details how a public web application combines information and game design to visualize effects of user-defined policies intended to reduce plastic waste.

arxiv-2403-12359.title: The Lyapunov exponent as a signature of dissipative many-body quantum chaos
arxiv-2403-12359.creator: Antonio M. Garc\́mathrm{i}a-Garc\́mathrm{i}a, Jacobus J. M. Verbaarschot, Jie-ping Zheng (郑杰平)
arxiv-2403-12359.description: Abstract A distinct feature of Hermitian quantum chaotic dynamics is the exponential increase of certain out-of-time-order-correlation (OTOC) functions around the Ehrenfest time with a rate given by a Lyapunov exponent. Physically, the OTOCs describe the growth of quantum uncertainty that crucially depends on the nature of the quantum motion.

arxiv-2404-11292.title: Sizes of the Nucleon
arxiv-2404-11292.creator: Norbert Kaiser, Wolfram Weise
arxiv-2404-11292.description: Abstract Evidences are updated and strengthened for the two-scales picture of low-energy nucleon structure as a compact ‘hard’ valence quark core surrounded by a ‘soft’ cloud of quark-antiquark pairs (the meson cloud). These considerations are quantified by a spectral analysis of the mean-squared radii associated with the isoscalar and isovector electric form factors of the nucleon.

arxiv-2505-05437.title: Cell size heterogeneity controls crystallization of the developing fruit fly wing
arxiv-2505-05437.creator: Kartik Chhajed, Franz S. Gruber, Raphaël Etournay, Natalie A. Dye, Frank Jülicher, Marko Popović
arxiv-2505-05437.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kartik Chhajed, Franz S. Gruber, Raphaël Etournay, Natalie A. Dye, Frank Jülicher, Marko Popović. A fundamental question in biology is to understand how patterns and shapes emerge from the collective interplay of large numbers of cells. Cells forming two-dimensional epithelial tissues behave as active materials that undergo remodeling and spontaneous shape changes. Focusing on the fly wing as a model system, we find that the cellular packing in the wing epithelium transitions from a disordered packing to an ordered, crystalline packing.

arxiv-2507-07873.title: Three-dimensional and clap-and-fling effects on a pair of flapping wings used for thrust generation
arxiv-2507-07873.creator: Antoine Papillon, Mathieu Olivier
arxiv-2507-07873.description: Abstract This research investigates the three-dimensional effects of flow around a pair of flapping wings undergoing clap-and-fling interactions through harmonic in-plane motions combining pitching, heaving, and deviation. Both wings mirror each other in their movements. Baseline parameters were selected based on efficient configurations from a previous two-dimensional study.

arxiv-2511-16593.title: Green Resilience of Cyber-Physical Systems
arxiv-2511-16593.creator: Diaeddin Rimawi
arxiv-2511-16593.description: Abstract Cyber-physical systems (CPS) integrate computational and physical components to interact with humans across various modalities. Online Collaborative Artificial Intelligence Systems (OL-CAIS) are a subset of CPS that collaborate with humans to achieve shared goals through online learning. These systems are exposed to environmental changes that may lead to performance degradation (i.e., disruptive events).

arxiv-2601-22688.title: TSLM: Tree-Structured Language Modeling for Divergent Thinking
arxiv-2601-22688.creator: Doyoung Kim, Jaehyeok Doo, Minjoon Seo
arxiv-2601-22688.description: Abstract Language models generate reasoning sequentially, preventing them from decoupling irrelevant exploration paths during search. We introduce Tree-Structured Language Modeling (TSLM), which uses special tokens to encode branching structure, enabling models to generate and selectively expand multiple search paths within a single generation process.

pmc-12430097.title: High-Purity Copper Recovery from Copper Sludge via Oxidative Refining Using a FeO–CaO–SiO2 Slag System
pmc-12430097.creator: Eunmi Park, Minji Kim, Young-Min Kim, Yong Hwan Kim, Balázs Illés
pmc-12430097.description: The rapid increase in electronic waste poses a significant environmental issue, with copper-rich residues considered among the most valuable fractions. Extracting copper of high purity from these materials is critical for advancing sustainable resource utilization. In this work, an oxidative refining approach employing a FeO–CaO–SiO2 slag matrix was investigated to purify copper-bearing sludge.

pmc-13376411.title: The influence of women’s empowerment on childhood vaccination coverage in Nigeria: a spatio-temporal analysis
pmc-13376411.creator: Ezra Gayawan, Osafu Augustine Egbon, Chigozie Edson Utazi, Jamila Abubakar Umar, Caroline Trotter
pmc-13376411.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Immunization is one of the most impactful public health achievements, significantly reducing childhood morbidity and mortality worldwide. However, gender disparity and women’s disempowerment constitute structural barriers in accessing vaccine services in low- and middle-income countries. In Nigeria, widespread differences in social norms and cultural values affect gender roles and influence women’s ability to decide their own healthcare needs and participate in household decision-making. This leads to attitudinal differences in uptake of immunization depending on the child’s location of residence.

pmc-13679754.creator: Hao Zhu, Chenggong Ma, Zhenchun Ran, Xumeng Liu, Haobo Tang, Tongquan Wu, Xinglong Wu, Yicheng Xie
pmc-13679754.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Spatial transcriptomics (ST) facilitates the spatial resolution of gene expression profiling; however, many widely used spot-based sequencing platforms capture transcripts from multiple neighboring cells at each location, producing mixed profiles that require accurate cell-type deconvolution. The wavelet-denoised graph attention framework for spatial transcriptomics deconvolution (WDGTA), a graph attention-based framework for ST cell-type deconvolution, was developed and validated on five datasets from two species and four organs.
